page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with no marginal notes. Running head at the top centre. Page number at the top right. Gathering signature and catchword at the foot.

main_text.p: catis, decreto libero hoc faceret. Atqui omnes actus pravi reproborum, omnes actus obedientiales electorum, Iesuitis, Dei liberum decretum & scientiam mediam antecedunt. At Deum libere efficere, ut id, quod est futurum antecedenter ad ipsius libertatem, non fit futurum, implicat contradictione sempiternam.

2. Si Deus extraordinarias vocationes cognoscit, quibus reprobi de facto converterentur, vel libere convertendi essent, vel necessario. Si libere, recurret argumentum idem pari robore. Si necessario, extra oleas disputatur. Conversio etenim laudabilis & obedientia Iesuitis erit non obedientialis & non necessaria. 3. Reducit totam Dei omnipotentiam ad impeditionem usus libertatis. Non ergo Dei dominium & omnipotentia facere possunt, ut plures libere convertantur, quam qui actu convertantur nec plures, non, converterentur & damnarentur, qua qui actu convertuntur. At si Dei dominium ad actus necessarios extenditur, pari etiam ratione ad actus liberos. Sed audi, Iupiter, Iesuitæ nostrũ Iehovam tecum catenis fati adamantinis alligarunt. 4 Hanc hypothesin esse impossibilem statuit Iesuita, quando dicit: Impossibile est ut sola voluntate refistat, sed infallibile erit, ut aliquo modo tentationis cadat. Satis innuit ad unum ictum tentationis, cor ad duos stare posse, & per eandem rationem, quia nulla tentatio determinat voluntatem, sed eam indifferentiae suae relinquit (alioqui ex Iesuitis, si necessitate peccatur, non peccatur omnino [?]).

page.notes: Printed page number at top right is faint: read as 515, doubtful. Paragraph break before "Reducit" is uncertain: the "3." sits at the end of the preceding line, so it is printed inline and I placed it at the start of the next sentence within the same paragraph. "Iesuitæ" and "Iesuitis" are read from a worn print that could also be "Iefuitæ"; spelling kept as best read. "omnino" closing the parenthesis is doubtful, and the word before it in the printed line is damaged. Italic passage: "Impossibile est ... cadat." Hyphenated "Im-" at the line end is printed as "Impossibile" joined in the transcription. Scan show-through and right-edge marks are not transcribed.
